heroStrategy.headline: Create High-Quality AI Images & Videos with ByteDance Generative Models
heroStrategy.subheadline: Unlock the power of next-generation generative AI with Seedream 4.5 and Seedance 1.5 Pro for professional visual content creation.
heroStrategy.designNote: Use a dark editorial hero with a full-bleed abstract AI background, overlaid by a centered content column and a prominent logo-first trust band beneath. Keep the composition unexpected by splitting the hero content into stacked editorial blocks rather than a standard split screen. Add precision grid lines, subtle orange glow edges, and a lightweight noise texture to make the interface feel premium and enterprise-grade. CTA must be solid orange with high contrast, and the hero should feel like a creative technology publication cover rather than a generic SaaS landing page.

repetitionBreakers: Centered editorial hero instead of split hero

Testimonials split into a mixed spotlight grid to break text rhythm
Final CTA framed as a product workflow canvas, not a plain form block
blueprint.pageTitle: Seedream 4.5 and Seedance 1.5 Pro | AI Image and Video Generation
blueprint.metaDescription: Create high-quality AI images and videos with ByteDance’s Seedream 4.5 and Seedance 1.5 Pro. Generate professional visuals, video, and synchronized audio with premium creative control.

sections.backgroundTreatment: dark editorial hero with layered typography blocks, precision-line grid, orange edge-light accents, and floating proof chips
sections.designNote: Hero must answer what it is, who it is for, and what to do next. Keep it content-first and premium, with a strong headline, concise supporting line, and a full-width solid orange CTA labeled 'Get started'. Use a compact visual layer behind the copy: abstract generative frame, subtle UI shell, and one product comparison chip to signal image + video generation without looking like a generic SaaS split hero.

Place trust immediately after the hero because the traffic is warm and the proof strategy is logos-first. Use a prominent static flex-wrap grid for 3-6 recognizable customer logos if available; since logos are not supplied, use a clean metric strip framed like editorial proof chips instead. Keep it visually dominant, compact, and highly legible.

Use a two-part product story with alternating layouts so the page does not feel repetitive. First product block: Seedream 4.5 in a tabs-with-preview shell, because it has 5 features and needs structured depth. Tabs should switch between text-to-image, editing, composition, typography, and fidelity views, with a polished browser-frame preview on the right. Second product block: Seedance 1.5 Pro as an accordion-with-visual or split-panel-list layout on a darker panel, emphasizing synchronized audio-video generation, lip-sync, cinematic camera control, and speed. Keep each block visually distinct while preserving one shared card system and accent color.

Since whyTechjockey is absent, repurpose this section as a lightweight confidence bridge: a compact editorial grid of buying considerations, support reassurance, and implementation benefits. Present as 3-4 cards with precision-line icons, not as a generic checklist. This section should reduce friction before pricing.

Show the two product plans as contrasted pricing cards rather than a table. Highlight Seedance 1.5 Pro as the more premium motion-focused offer, but keep both equally credible. Use one solid orange CTA per card labeled 'Get started'. Include the starting price for Seedance and a quote-led structure for Seedream. Keep pricing visually clean and enterprise-appropriate, with no noisy badges.

With 5 testimonials, use a mixed 3-card grid plus a secondary row or spotlight card rather than a carousel. Prioritize quotes from Creative Director, Video Producer, and Art Director for relevance. Present each as a refined proof card with author, role, and a concise pull-quote. Avoid repeating the same card dimensions in a strict pattern—vary one featured quote larger than the others to create rhythm.

Final conversion moment should feel like a premium action canvas, not a basic form. Use a floating product workflow card with a short closing message and a single full-width orange CTA labeled 'Get started'. Since warm traffic prefers low-friction next steps, keep the form minimal and avoid multiple CTA variants. The visual should echo the hero and close the loop with the same design language.

Do not use a marquee because the rules forbid auto-scrolling logos unless explicitly requested. If a news/media area is needed, render it as a static horizontal logo strip or omit entirely. Keep it understated and consistent with the trust system.

blueprint.designPersonality: An editorial, premium B2B AI landing page with strong contrast, orange-led identity, and a trust-first structure. It feels more like a high-end creative tech publication than a generic SaaS page, with dominant proof, refined spacing, and intelligent visual hierarchy.
blueprint.imageryDirection: Use polished abstract AI visuals, product-style shells, editorial mockups, and cinematic motion frames. Favor dark surfaces with orange edge light, precise grid accents, and layered content panels. Every visual must be framed as a browser shell, dashboard card, workflow canvas, or bento container. Avoid raw screenshots and avoid any media that contains unrelated product branding or text.

referenceMap.heroPattern: Single-screen split hero with brand/logo at top-left, large bold headline, short supporting paragraph, and a compact bullet list of key value points. Visual emphasis comes from typography and clear hierarchy rather than imagery.
referenceMap.sectionRhythm: Top hero/banner followed by a lead-capture form block, then informational product sections stacked vertically. Content progression is linear and sales-oriented, with repeated headline-description-feature patterns.
referenceMap.cardStyle: Simple boxed content cards/containers with strong borders or subtle separation, minimal decoration, and utility-first layout. Primary content is text-heavy with small icon accents for bullets and checks.
referenceMap.ctaPattern: Primary CTA appears in the hero and repeated in feature/product sections. CTAs are direct and action-oriented, with form-first conversion behavior supported by a dedicated lead form area.
referenceMap.pricingPattern: No visible pricing module in the provided reference structure; pricing is not a dominant layout pattern in this page.
referenceMap.footerMode: Footer is not included in the provided HTML excerpt, so no reusable footer pattern can be confirmed.
referenceMap.mediaPattern: Minimal media usage in the shown structure; brand logo in the hero and small inline icons for bullets/ticks. No large product imagery, video, or gallery module is evident.
referenceMap.productSectionPattern: Each product section follows a repeatable pattern: label tag, product name/headline, paragraph description, then a structured feature list. Content is stacked vertically with progressive disclosure via section separation rather than tabs or accordions.
referenceMap.formPattern: Dedicated lead form card placed near the top of the page. Uses a prominent title, hidden tracking fields, and utility form structure optimized for conversion and lead capture.
referenceMap.animationStyle: Static, enterprise-style presentation with no explicit motion system visible in the provided markup. If used, motion should remain minimal and functional rather than decorative.
componentPatterns: bullet benefit list with tick icons
designNotes: Prioritize text hierarchy and conversion flow over decorative visuals.
Use compact, trust-building bullet lists in the hero.
Keep sections vertically stacked and easy to scan.
Use repeated CTA placement across the page for lead generation.
Favor utility containers and straightforward enterprise styling.
Reserve imagery for brand marks and lightweight icons unless stronger visual proof is needed.

mustHaveMoments: Sticky top banner strip with prominent logo/trust area for the entire page

Repeat CTA after each major product section to support demo-driven conversion
Separate product blocks for Seedream 4.5 and Seedance 1.5 Pro with structured feature lists
Pricing/quote-focused section that reinforces request-demo intent rather than self-serve purchase
Testimonial block with role-specific quotes from creative and marketing decision-makers
Final conversion section that restates outcomes and invites quote/demo request
avoidPatterns: Do not use a form in the hero unless explicitly provided in the content map
Do not leave empty visual space on the hero; keep the layout grounded and complete
Do not make the page feel like a generic AI gimmick; keep it enterprise and premium
Do not overuse decorative media or irrelevant abstract visuals
Do not rely on badges alone as proof; logos should dominate trust
Do not bury product differentiation inside long paragraphs without scannable structure
Do not use a centered hero if it weakens the conversion hierarchy for this audience
designStrategy.reasoning: This landing page should behave like a high-intent, sales-led product category page for enterprise buyers evaluating advanced generative AI tools. The content is solution-aware and strongly product-specific, so the best approach is product-led with a premium, efficient tone and a split hero that prioritizes message clarity over heavy visuals. Because the audience trusts logos most, trust must be built through a dominant logo-first strategy, ideally supported by a visible sticky top strip and a strong trust band near the top. Conversion intent is demo/quote oriented rather than transactional, so CTA language should stay medium-strength and repeated at key decision points. The content is dense and technical, so the layout should remain structured and scannable, with distinct product sections for image and video capabilities, plus proof and pricing moments that help enterprise evaluation.

strengths: Design planned from strategy and intent layers
